result:
result: holycodex v0.16.12 has 7 capabilities and a registry for them. HolyAgent has booleans, not a registry. Only `computer_use` has a direct HolyAgent counterpart; the rest have none or are inferred.

Sourced facts are from the local clone at `/home/user/davidbasilefilho/holycodex`. Its `packages/cli/package.json` reads 0.16.12. I had no shell, so I could not confirm that the working tree is at commit a56aa72 or that it is clean.

**holycodex v0.16.12: sourced from `packages/core/src/capabilities.ts`**

The registry is `CAPABILITY_REGISTRY: Record<CapabilityName, CapabilityDefinition>`. Each entry has `pluginIds`, `defaultSelected`, `semanticSkillIds`, `applicability` and `ownership: "shared-preserve"`. Defaults are in `DEFAULT_CAPABILITY_SELECTIONS`.

| Capability | Grants | Default | Toggle |
|---|---|---|---|
| `frontend` | Plugin `build-web-apps@openai-curated`. Skills: frontend-app-builder, frontend-testing-debugging, react-best-practices, projected into Root instructions via `CAPABILITY_APPLICABILITY`. | on, required (`REQUIRED_CAPABILITY_NAMES`) | none |
| `security` | Plugin `codex-security@openai-curated`. Skills: security-diff-scan, security-scan, threat-model. | on, required | none |
| `browser_use` | Plugin list is empty: it is host-managed by Codex Desktop, and the CLI never installs it. It adds a Browser Use sentence to Root and specialist instructions and an in-app browser (IAB) visual fallback. | on | `--browser-use` / `--no-browser-use` (`args.ts` `INSTALL_OPTION_CATALOG`) |
| `sites` | Plugin `sites@openai-bundled`. | on | `--sites` / `--no-sites` |
| `computer_use` | Plugin `computer-use@openai-bundled`, skill `computer-use:computer-use`, and a Computer Use sentence in specialist instructions. | off | `--computer-use` / `--no-computer-use` |
| `session-audit` | Skill `session-audit` for token, cache and context audits (`docs/BEHAVIOR.md` line 312). | off | wizard Space toggle only (`installer-wizard.ts` `toggleCapability`); no CLI flag in `args.ts` |
| `auto-reset` | Skill `auto-reset` for quota thresholds and banked reset (`docs/BEHAVIOR.md` line 319). | off | wizard only |

- **Scope:** Capabilities are global per install, recorded in the active record as `optional_selections` and `capability_state`. They are not per role or per task.
- **Where they reach agents:** Only `browserUse` and `computerUse` reach specialists, through `NativeAgentCapabilityOptions` and `renderNativeAgent` in `native-agents.ts`. The Worker.visual and Reviewer.visual agents also get the frontend instruction. `sessionAudit` and `autoReset` only reach Root.
- **Persistence:** `InstalledOptionalCapabilitySelectionsSchema` defaults `session-audit` and `auto-reset` to false for older records. `resolveOptionalCapabilitySelections` makes an omitted flag inherit the previous value, then the default. `migrateOptionalCapabilitySelections` converts an old record to the current shape and drops the legacy `work` capability.
- **Dependencies:** No capability depends on another. `docs/CONFIGURATION.md` lines 124-136 say plugins resolve only for the selected set.
- **Prerequisites:** `capabilityHealth(selected, providerStatus)` returns healthy, missing, disabled or uncertain. The docs say an unavailable selected capability fails the install explicitly, with no silent omission.
- **Doctor:** `doctorHolyCodexEffect` in `maintenance.ts` runs a `capabilities` check. It fails with `selected_capability_not_healthy` and names the first selected non-healthy capability, skipping `browser_use`. `browser_use` gets its own `unsupported` check with the reason `surface_managed_by_codex_desktop`.
- **Setup UI:** The wizard has an OPTIONAL CAPABILITIES section. `renderInstall` in `commands.ts` prints each selected capability with its status.
- **No effect:** None of the capabilities touches model routing or MCP servers.

**HolyAgent side: sourced from `/home/user/holyagent-0.3.0-t3branch/packages/runtime/src/config/`**

- **Switches:** `schema.ts` defines `pi.enable` (default true) and `pi.features`. `pi.features` has `web` (one of `provider`, `pi-web-kit` or `off`, default `provider`), plus the booleans `processes`, `todo`, `ask`, `mcp`, `computerUse`, `contextCompression` and `subagents`, all default true.
- **Other settings:** `pi.codemode` has `mode` (`on` or `only`, default `only`) and `maxWorkers`. `pi.t3` has `scope`, `worktrees` and `deviceAccess`. `pi.routes` holds the per-role model table.
- **Pinned packages** (`pi-packages.json`): `pi-provider-kimi-code`, `@tintinweb/pi-subagents`, `billion-context`, `@juicesharp/rpiv-todo`, `@juicesharp/rpiv-ask-user-question`, `@aliou/pi-processes`, `@amaster.ai/pi-computer-use` and `pi-web-kit`.
- **No registry:** There is no capability registry, no doctor check and no way to attach a switch to a role.

**Mapping**

| holycodex | HolyAgent counterpart |
|---|---|
| `computer_use` | `pi.features.computerUse`, already default true (holycodex defaults it off). Package: `@amaster.ai/pi-computer-use`. |
| `browser_use` | No existing switch. The assignment names opencode browse as a planned piece; I could not read the 0.3.1 plan. |
| `sites` | None. It is an OpenAI-hosted service. |
| `frontend` | None. There are no HolyAgent skills for it, and the OpenAI plugins do not exist in Pi. |
| `security` | None. The assignment's "Codex auto-review" may cover it, but I could not read that plan. |
| `session-audit` | None. Billion Context (`features.contextCompression`) is related but is context compression, not an audit. |
| `auto-reset` | None. It depends on the Codex quota RPC, which Pi lacks. |
| The screen capability, just-bash TS/JS and fff from the 0.3.1 plan | holycodex has no equivalent. I did not read these plans. |

**Inference (not sourced)**

- A matching system is a `pi.capabilities` map or a registry keyed by name, with a default and `requires` metadata, that drives the existing `features` switches. It would keep each capability's packages, skills and doctor check in one definition, so a new capability is one entry.
- "Most default enabled" fits HolyAgent's all-true feature defaults. holycodex itself has three of five optional capabilities off by default.
